title: When Attention Sink Emerges in Language Models: An Empirical View

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution aims to establish that attention sink (large attention to the first token) is a universal, pre-training-emergent phenomenon in auto-regressive LMs. Paper [1] explicitly explores the presence of attention sink in the initial token, describing it as receiving disproportionately large attention scores despite its lack of semantic importance. While [1] delves into the phenomenon, it does not establish universality across LM families or pre-training emergence. Paper [10] mentions attention sinking but focuses on spectral filters and does not address universality or pre-training emergence. No prior paper establishes the same empirical relationship across models and training stages.

### Mechanism
The contribution uses an empirical measurement approach with the Sink_k^epsilon metric to track attention sink emergence across LM families and pre-training checkpoints. Paper [1] discusses attention sink but does not use a metric like Sink_k^epsilon or track emergence over pre-training checkpoints. Paper [10] mentions attention sinking but focuses on spectral filters and does not employ a comparable metric or methodology. No prior paper employs a substantively equivalent mechanism for measuring and tracking attention sink emergence.

### Evaluation
The evaluation demonstrates attention sink universality across inputs, models, and pre-training stages, and analyzes the first token's key manifold properties. Paper [1] evaluates attention sink but does not establish universality across inputs or models, nor does it analyze the first token's key manifold properties. Paper [10] discusses attention sinking but does not use the same evaluation design or metrics. No prior paper uses the same evaluation design to validate universality and emergence.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of LLM interpretability and transformer attention. Paper [1] and Paper [10] both address attention phenomena in LLMs, which falls within the same general application area. While the specific focus differs, the domain is covered.
